capa.title:
PNI Sanitation
Dominican Republic
capa.subtitle: Investment estimate (CAPEX) to achieve universal urban wastewater collection and treatment by 2040, using spatial data analysis and the SaniPLAN model.

ato0.title: How much does it cost to achieve universal urban sanitation in the Dominican Republic?

s1.title: A model at the center
items: SaniPLAN calculates the investment required to reach a coverage target.
Spatial data generate the parameters for each district.
The results show where the needs are and what they cost.

s2.title: We start with the data
items: Censuses, satellite imagery, streets, buildings and network records.
Each source has a different level of aggregation.
Spatial analysis turns these sources into indicators by district.

node.saniplan: Population, coverage and investment projection model

detail.censo: Total and urban population by municipal district in the last three censuses. Basis for the baseline and the projection to 2040.
detail.sat: Used to validate global population sources and to check urban areas that the census classifies as rural.
detail.ruas: Street length in each urban area. It is the proxy indicator for sewer network length per connection.
detail.edif: Footprint of each building (25 to 500 m²). Used to estimate households per connection and to correct the population distribution.
detail.cad: Areas served by existing networks (records and projects) and sewer coverage by province.
detail.custos: Reference costs for networks, connections, WWTPs, outfalls and on-site solutions. Targets: coverage % and year.
detail.spatial: 10-ha hexagonal grid for the whole country. Each hexagon receives population, buildings and streets, and is then aggregated by district.
detail.saniplan: Excel spreadsheet that projects population and coverage year by year and calculates the CAPEX for collection, conveyance and treatment by district.
detail.capex: Total investment and investment per inhabitant, split between sewer network and treatment.
detail.charts: Annual evolution of the population served and of investment up to the target year.
detail.map: Results aggregated by province and region, the level with the best reliability.
detail.decide: Compare needs and costs across regions to rank programs and projects.

ato1.title: The data required
ato1.lead: A national plan depends on where people live, how the city is built and where service already exists.

problema.title: The problem with aggregated data
items: Many plans use averages by municipality or by country.
An average hides where the population actually is.
Network costs depend on density and street layout, which vary within a single district.

grid.title: One value per district × a 100 m grid
items: By district: the census population applies to the whole polygon, including empty areas.
By hexagon: the same population distributed across the hexagons where there are buildings.
The district total is preserved. What changes is knowing where people are.

fontes.title: Sources and levels of aggregation
items: Each dot shows the most detailed level at which the data exist.
Population is available at fine scale. Sewer coverage, only by province. Treatment, only as a national average.
The result is never more precise than the most aggregated data used in the calculation.
fontes.note: Hollow dot = partial data (only in some districts).

ato2.title: Spatial analysis
ato2.lead: From the country to the city block, and back to the district.

niveis.title: From the country to the district
items: Country: 32 provinces, 393 municipal districts.
Province: the level at which sewer coverage data exist.
District: the level of the census and of the SaniPLAN parameters.
We will zoom in on Santo Domingo Este, in Santo Domingo province.

hex.title: Why a 10-ha hexagonal grid
items: Same area everywhere in the country: indicators are comparable across places.
Hexagons have 6 equidistant neighbors, which makes it easier to detect urban continuity.
10 ha reduces the noise of point data and keeps sub-district detail.
486,526 hexagons cover the country; 1,311 in Santo Domingo Este.
hex.hint: Click a hexagon to see its indicators.

ghs.title: Correcting the modeled population
items: The global grid (GHSL) sometimes places population in industrial or empty areas.
Red: population without buildings → population set to zero.
Blue: buildings without population → buildings × inhabitants per household.
The 2022 census population is then redistributed proportionally.

censo.title: An inconsistency in the census
items: Between 2010 and 2022 the country's rural population grew by about 550,000, against the urbanization trend.
In Santo Domingo Este, the rural population went from 40,099 to 116,935 (+192%).
Blue: official urban area. Amber: area that the census classifies as rural.
The imagery shows why: the area classified as rural has been urbanized.
censo.swipe: Drag the slider to compare 2010 and 2022

reclass.title: Reclassifying what is already city
items: Blue: official urban area (ONE, 2021).
Amber: hexagons with more than 100 buildings and at least 50% of neighbors built up.
In Santo Domingo Este: 148 hexagons, ~100,000 inhabitants and 23,944 buildings now count as urban.
Nationwide, the urban population considered is 860,000 above the census.

indic.title: Indicators by district
items: Street meters per building: proxy indicator for meters of network per connection.
Families per building: indicator of households per connection (verticalization).
Calculated only in consolidated urban areas and filtered to remove extreme values.
These values feed into SaniPLAN for each district.
indic.hint: Click a district to see the values used in the model.

cobertura.title: Current coverage
items: Sewer coverage exists only by province (ENHOGAR 2021 / Census 2022).
Where network records exist, the population served was recalculated within the network area.
Coverage in the remaining districts is adjusted to preserve the province total.
Treatment: national average of ~50% of the wastewater collected.

hexsat.title: The hexagons over the 2022 imagery
items: Each amber hexagon lies outside the official urban area but has more than 100 buildings and built-up neighbors.
On the imagery, the street and block pattern appears where the census records rural area.
The reclassification follows what is seen on the ground, not the administrative boundary.
hexsat.hint: Click a hexagon to see buildings, streets and population.

ato3.title: SaniPLAN
ato3.lead: Excel model to project population, coverage and investment from municipal or district data.
ato3.authors: Model by Pery Nazareth. Application to the Dominican Republic and spatial analysis by Leonardo Nazareth.

subnav.hint: The buttons reproduce the spreadsheet's navigation bar and lead to each scene in this part.

fluxo.title: Model flow
fluxo.lead: Four steps, always in the same order. Each district is a row; each year, a column.

in.title: Inputs
items: List of municipalities or districts
Current population and previous censuses
Current collection and treatment coverage
Reference unit costs
Targets: coverage % and year
Adjustment parameters

sub.title: Sub-models
items: Year-by-year population projection
Redistribution of provincial coverage among districts
Unit costs adjusted by city size, construction difficulty and treatment level

calc.title: Annual calculation
items: 2024 baseline → target, in equal steps
New households and inhabitants each year
Increment × unit cost = CAPEX for the year

out.title: Results
items: Population served by year
Coverage by year
CAPEX by component: network, connections, conveyance, treatment, minimum sanitary facilities

shots.lb: LB: baseline by district (population, coverage, targets)
shots.calc: CALC: parameters and unit costs by district
shots.result: <RESULT>: national summary and table by province

fluxo.flow4: Sequence diagram of the <INICIO> sheet: parameters → baseline and targets → coverage and investment calculation → results report.

pob.title: Population projection
pob.lead: Five candidate curves per district. The choice depends on how many censuses exist and on the shape of the trend.

methods.title: Methods
items: Logistic: grows toward a saturation population.
Decreasing rate: growth that slows over time.
Gompertz: asymmetric S-curve; the most used (374 districts).
Linear: constant increment per year.
Geometric: constant rate per year.

matrix.title: Selection matrix
matrix.intro: The three censuses (2002, 2010, 2022) define the case; each case has an order of preference for the short and long term.

matrix.note: Districts created after 2002 or 2010 have their population redistributed to the 2022 boundaries and use only two data points.

calib.title: National calibration
items: The sum of the districts was adjusted year by year to the official national projection (ONE).
Urbanization: 86.88% of the total population in 2040.
Baseline: 8,875,227 urban inhabitants in 2024.

chart.hint: Hover over the chart to read the values.

custos.title: Unit costs
custos.lead: Reference costs loaded in the model and adjusted by district. Users can replace them with their own.

rede.title: Sewer network
items: Two types: conventional (AC) and simplified (AE).
Three levels of construction difficulty: low, medium, high. In the metropolitan district, always high.
Cost per connection = m of network per connection × $/m + house connection + transport factor (trunk sewers, pumping).
Densification (infill): 10% of new connections are served by the existing network (−10%).
m of network per connection and households per connection come from the spatial analysis (Part 2).
head: Difficulty
AC network $/m
AE network $/m
AC house conn. $/conn.
AE house conn. $/conn.
rede.photoAC: Conventional network: deep trenches, larger-diameter pipes.
rede.photoAE: Simplified (condominial) network: shallow, small-diameter pipes, short house connections.
rede.desglose: Breakdown of the unit cost per meter (services, materials, indirect costs), basis of the cost module.

ete.title: Treatment
items: Cost curve by load: $/kg BOD₅·day = 35,000 × load<sup>−0.303</sup>. The larger the plant, the lower the cost per kg.
Based on actual WWTP costs in Latin America and the Caribbean.
Four treatment levels, with a factor applied to the curve: primary ×0.25, basic ×0.60, intermediate ×1.00, advanced ×1.25.
Required BOD removal: 85–88% inland, 67–77% on the coast. It defines the level.
Per capita load: 40, 50 or 60 g BOD/inhab·day, by city size.

emis.title: Submarine outfall
items: Six coastal districts with more than 100,000 inhabitants: Puerto Plata, Bajos de Haina, La Romana, San Pedro de Macorís, Santo Domingo de Guzmán and Santo Domingo Este.
Cost per meter as a function of diameter, estimated from population; added to the WWTP cost per inhabitant.

insitu.title: On-site solutions and minimum facilities
items: On-site: containment (dry or flush toilet) and septic sludge treatment. Target = 100% sewered, so on-site sanitation is not included in the scenarios.
ISM (minimum household sanitary facilities): 19% of new connected households × USD 1,484.51, from 2025 to 2034.
Shown separately in the results: they are neither network nor treatment.

size.title: Size matters
size.lead: The 2024 population defines the district's size band. The band defines construction difficulty, network cost, transport factor, per capita load and treatment level.

sim.lead: JavaScript replica of the CALC and RESULTADOS sheets, with the spreadsheet's exact calculation chain. Change the yellow cells and the scenario in red; the rest is fixed.

sim.note: Target applied equally to collection and treatment. Time horizon = target year − 2024. Unit costs, population band and WWTP load are defined by the 2024 population, as in the spreadsheet. Values in 2024 USD.

res.title: Model results
items: Coverage, population served and investment by year, from 2025 to the target year.
Calculated by district and aggregable by province and region, the level with the best reliability.
Separated by component: network, treatment, minimum facilities. This is what Part 4 presents.

submod.title: Two sub-modules feed SaniPLAN
submod.lead: They are independent spreadsheets. They run before the model and deliver two baseline inputs to it: the projected population of each district and the unit costs adjusted to the country and to the population band.

ato4.lead: Investment to serve 90% or 100% of the urban population with sewer collection and treatment by 2040. Choose the scenario and the indicator; click a province to see the detail.
